description: RAJAR, Radio Joint Audience Research, is the official body that measures radio listening in the United Kingdom, jointly owned by the BBC and Radiocentre on behalf of commercial radio, and responsible for audience figures since 1992. Respondents keep a diary in which they record, by quarter hour, any listening of at least five minutes to a station, along with the platform, such as FM, AM, DAB, digital television or online, and the place of listening. From these RAJAR estimates each station's weekly reach, the number of people listening for at least five consecutive minutes in a week, weekly listening hours and share of all radio listening in its service area, for more than 300 stations, with results for 3, 6 or 12 month periods depending on station size and for areas from 50,000 adults to the whole population. Quarterly topline figures are published free on the website; detailed data by demographic group and time of day are available only to subscribers such as stations, agencies and licensed bureaux. Coverage: United Kingdom, quarterly since 1992. Format and access: web tables free; detailed data by subscription. Caveats: diary methods under-record short listening; online and podcast measurement is still developing. Simulation uses: demand for broadcast services by platform and region, reach of radio for emergency messages when other networks fail, and behaviour inputs for agent-based models. Related records: the Eurobarometer e-communications survey covers households across Europe.
